brief: S&P failed to break out of a two month range near 7700, with the gap higher in yields blamed for the failure. The index is back at 7700. The author advises pairing significant long equity exposure with a simply expressed trading short in bonds, and credits the stock market for not giving up ground against the rate move. Separately, Meta's Muse is framed as another inflection in agentic AI, priced quickly by mega cap tech stocks. Trader Rich Privorotsky argues Muse is the first of many entrants that will change productivity, and that the aggregate effect is positive for equities and structurally disinflationary, alongside more expected volatility. A GS portfolio strategy note finds the market has partially priced skepticism about AI infrastructure earnings growth durability: the median AI infrastructure stock has de-rated from 32x consensus forward earnings in April 2026 to 22x today. Small caps have underperformed the S&P for six weeks on selling from long only funds and the wealth channel plus rate driven tightening in financial conditions, and the NDX versus RTY ratio has made a new high. On positioning, buybacks are slowing, new issue is rising, and speculative length sits at +3 on a -10 to +10 scale.
